subject: Venezuela oil agreement gains disclosed 25-year field and production scope
body_md: Thesis: SUPERSEDE prior state AGREEMENT_ANNOUNCED + SANCTIONS_RAILS_OPEN -> AGREEMENT_SCOPE_DISCLOSED + COMMERCIAL_EXECUTION_ENABLED, while PHYSICAL_PRODUCTION_UPLIFT remains unconfirmed. Venezuela's Foreign Ministry/Prensa Presidencial reports the U.S.-Venezuela binational energy project is signed for 25 years, covers 17 strategic fields, and targets production above 1.5 million bpd; Venezuela says the structure preserves state sovereignty over reserves and relies on U.S. capital/technology. Independent corroboration: Reuters Aug 30 reports interim President Delcy Rodriguez announced the 25-year agreement and the 1.5m bpd target. This materially improves contract-duration and field-scope certainty versus the previous political announcement, but does not prove capex deployment, operator contracts, rigs, or incremental barrels. Confidence: +0.87 on disclosed agreement scope; +0.48 on meaningful incremental production within 12 months. Counterevidence: degraded infrastructure, financing/execution risk, legal/political durability risk, and no observed production uplift yet. First-order impact: increases probability of sustained U.S./foreign operator participation and service/capital flows. Second-order impact: raises Venezuela's medium-term relevance as a non-Hormuz heavy-crude supply source and Gulf Coast refining input. Falsifier: controlling U.S./Venezuelan documents materially narrow the announced scope; field/operator contracts fail to close; capex/rig/diluent/tanker data do not respond; or production does not show sustained improvement over the implementation window. Evidence: https://mppre.gob.ve/index.php/publicacion/7986 ; https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/venezuelas-interim-president-says-us-energy-deal-will-last-25-years-2026-08-30/ . Reality Clause: advisory only; no trade or capital action authorized.
